title: Class Sheet — Sem 8
intro: Every exercise of the Sem-8 sheet: **negative numbers** (+ − × ÷), **powers** with brackets, comparing, **dates before Christ**, and the grammar of **tout** (déterminant, adverbe, pronom).

hints: Start at 4 on the number line and go 7 steps down (left).

traps.0: The distance is 3, but you cross zero: the result is negative.
traps.3: −11 would be −4 − 7. Here you start at +4.

solution: Start at 4, move 7 to the left: 4 → 0 takes 4 steps, 3 more steps go below zero.
questions.idea: Subtracting a bigger number goes below zero.

hints: 3 steps down reach 0, 2 more go below.

traps.0: Right size, wrong sign: you went past zero.

solution: 3 − 5: bigger number is being subtracted, so the answer is negative.
questions.idea: Smaller − bigger = negative.

hints: Start at −2 and go 4 steps up (right).

traps.0: −6 would be −2 − 4. Here you ADD 4.
traps.1: Adding 4 moves you right of zero: −2 + 4 is positive (4 is bigger than 2).

solution: Start at −2, move 4 to the right: 2 steps to 0, 2 more steps → **2**.
questions.idea: Adding a positive moves right.

hints: Start below zero and keep going down.
Same sign: add 9 + 15, keep the minus.

traps.0: You subtracted 15 − 9. Both move you down, so add them.
traps.3: You are below zero: the answer is negative.

solution: Both numbers push you DOWN: −9, then 15 more steps down.
questions.idea: Same sign: add the sizes, keep the sign.

traps.0: Different signs give a NEGATIVE product.
traps.1: You added (2 + −3 = −1…). This is a multiplication.

solution: The signs are different (+ and −) → negative → **−6**
questions.idea: Different signs → negative.

hints: Divide 35 by 7 first, then think about the sign.

traps.0: −35 + 7 would give −28. Here you divide.
traps.1: Different signs give a negative result.

questions.idea: Same sign rules for × and ÷.

hints: Work from left to right, one step at a time.

traps.0: You treated + −22 as + 22. Adding a negative is the same as subtracting.
traps.2: You stopped before the last number.

traps.1: You subtracted 10. But 81 − (−10) = 81 + 10: minus a negative is a plus.

questions.idea: Multiply first. Minus a negative = plus.

traps.0: Five negative factors: an ODD number, so the result is negative.
traps.2: −2 × 5 = −10 is multiplication. A power means repeated multiplication: 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2.

questions.idea: Odd number of negatives → negative.

hints: No brackets: only the 2 is raised to the power 5.

traps.1: The minus stays: −(2⁵) = −32.
traps.2: A power is repeated multiplication, not 2 × 5.

solution: No brackets → the minus is NOT part of the base.
Same answer as (−2)⁵ here, because 5 is odd.
questions.idea: No brackets: the power acts on the number only.

hints: A minus in front of a negative number flips it.

traps.0: Two minus signs cancel.

questions.idea: Minus a negative = plus.

hints: Three minus signs: odd number → negative.

traps.0: Count the minus signs: three (odd) → negative.

questions.idea: Odd number of minus signs → negative.

traps.0: (−2)⁵ is negative (5 negatives). 51 + 32 = 83 treats it as positive.
traps.1: Check the multiplication: −17 × −3 is positive (51), not negative.

questions.idea: Order: brackets, powers, × ÷, then + −.

hints: Do each power first. (−2)⁴ has brackets: the base is −2.

traps.0: −3² is −9, not +9: with no brackets only the 3 is squared, then the minus is applied.

questions.idea: Brackets decide what is raised to the power.

questions.text: **Exercice 3 a)**  Inscrivez le signe <, = ou >  :  (−4)³  ___  −4³
hints: Compare the two numbers on the number line.

traps.0: Compute each side: (−4)³ = −64 and −4³ = −(4 × 4 × 4) = −64.

questions.idea: Compute both sides, then compare.

questions.text: **Exercice 3 b)**  Inscrivez le signe <, = ou >  :  −7²  ___  (−7)²
hints: Compare the two numbers on the number line.

traps.1: Compute each side: −7² = −49 (no brackets) and (−7)² = +49.

questions.idea: Compute both sides, then compare.

questions.text: **Exercice 3 c)**  Inscrivez le signe <, = ou >  :  −(−3)³  ___  −3³
hints: Compare the two numbers on the number line.

traps.0: Compute each side: (−3)³ = −27 so −(−3)³ = +27, and −3³ = −27.
traps.1: Compute each side: (−3)³ = −27 so −(−3)³ = +27, and −3³ = −27.

questions.idea: Compute both sides, then compare.

questions.text: **Exercice 3 d)**  Inscrivez le signe <, = ou >  :  (−8)⁰  ___  −8⁰
hints: Compare the two numbers on the number line.

traps.0: Anything (not zero) to the power 0 is 1: (−8)⁰ = 1, but −8⁰ = −(8⁰) = −1.
traps.1: Anything (not zero) to the power 0 is 1: (−8)⁰ = 1, but −8⁰ = −(8⁰) = −1.

questions.idea: Compute both sides, then compare.

questions.text: **Exercice 4 · 1)** Le chef gaulois Vercingétorix est né en **−72** (72 avant Jésus-Christ) et il vécut jusqu’en **−46**. Combien d’années a-t-il vécu ?
hints: How long = end year − birth year.

traps.0: 72 + 46 adds the two years. But both are BC: the years get closer to zero, so you subtract: 72 − 46.
traps.2: A duration is never negative: end − start = −46 − (−72) = +26.
traps.3: 72 is the birth year, not the number of years lived.

solution: On the timeline: from −72 up to −46 is 26 steps.
questions.idea: Duration = end − start (the minus a negative becomes a plus).

questions.text: **Exercice 4 · 2)** Le géomètre Euclide est né en **−323** et est décédé en **−283**. Quel âge avait-il à sa mort ?
hints: Age at death = death year − birth year.

traps.0: 323 + 283 adds. Subtract the earlier year from the later one.
traps.1: An age is positive: −283 − (−323) = +40.
traps.3: 323 is the birth year, not his age.

questions.idea: Duration = end − start.

questions.text: **Ex 1 · 1.**  Elle prend des cours de danse ………… les jours.
hints: Look at the NOUN after the blank: *tout* is a déterminant and agrees with it in gender and number.

traps.0: *jours* is plural: *tout* is for singular.

questions.idea: Tout: determiner → agrees with the noun · pronoun → agrees with what it stands for · adverb → only before a feminine adjective starting with a consonant / h aspiré.

questions.text: **Ex 2 · 1.**  Ils sont ………… émus !
hints: Before an ADJECTIVE, *tout* is an adverb: invariable, except before a FEMININE adjective that starts with a consonne or an h aspiré — then it agrees (toute / toutes).
*émus* is masculine and starts with a vowel.

traps.1: An adverb before a masculine adjective is invariable, even if the subject is plural.

solution: *émus* is masculine (and starts with a vowel) → *tout* stays invariable: **tout** émus.
questions.idea: Tout: determiner → agrees with the noun · pronoun → agrees with what it stands for · adverb → only before a feminine adjective starting with a consonant / h aspiré.

*droit* is a masculine adjective used as an adverb.
questions.idea: Tout: determiner → agrees with the noun · pronoun → agrees with what it stands for · adverb → only before a feminine adjective starting with a consonant / h aspiré.

questions.text: **Ex 2 · 3.**  Sonia est ………… seule à la maison ce soir !

*seule* is feminine and starts with the consonant s.

traps.0: The adjective is feminine and starts with a consonant: *tout* must agree.

solution: *seule* is feminine and starts with a consonant → agrees: **toute** seule.
questions.idea: Tout: determiner → agrees with the noun · pronoun → agrees with what it stands for · adverb → only before a feminine adjective starting with a consonant / h aspiré.

questions.text: **Ex 2 · 9.**  Claire est ………… étonnée de son succès.
hints: Before an ADJECTIVE, *tout* is an adverb: invariable, except before a FEMININE adjective that starts with a consonne or an h aspiré — then it agrees (toute / toutes).
*étonnée* is feminine but starts with a VOWEL.

traps.2: Before a vowel the adverb stays invariable (it would sound the same anyway: *tout-t…*).

solution: *étonnée* is feminine but starts with a vowel → invariable: **tout** étonnée.
questions.idea: Tout: determiner → agrees with the noun · pronoun → agrees with what it stands for · adverb → only before a feminine adjective starting with a consonant / h aspiré.

questions.text: **Ex 2 · 10.**  Ces étudiantes sont ………… heureuses de leur résultat de l’examen !
hints: Before an ADJECTIVE, *tout* is an adverb: invariable, except before a FEMININE adjective that starts with a consonne or an h aspiré — then it agrees (toute / toutes).
*heureuses* starts with a silent h (h muet): it counts as a vowel.

traps.3: Only h ASPIRÉ counts as a consonant. *heureuses* has an h muet.

solution: *heureuses* starts with an h muet = a vowel sound → invariable: **tout** heureuses.
questions.idea: Tout: determiner → agrees with the noun · pronoun → agrees with what it stands for · adverb → only before a feminine adjective starting with a consonant / h aspiré.

questions.text: **Pronom 1.**  Ne t’inquiète pas pour les bagages, ………… suit. (sens collectif)
hints: Before a VERB, *tout* is a pronoun. Collective meaning = singular.

traps.1: *Tous suivent* means “all the bags”, with the verb in the plural. Here the verb is *suit* (singular).

questions.idea: Tout: determiner → agrees with the noun · pronoun → agrees with what it stands for · adverb → only before a feminine adjective starting with a consonant / h aspiré.

questions.text: **Pronom 2.**  Ne t’inquiète pas pour les valises, ………… suivent. (toutes les valises)
hints: Before a verb → pronoun: it agrees with what it replaces.

traps.1: *valises* is feminine.

questions.idea: Tout: determiner → agrees with the noun · pronoun → agrees with what it stands for · adverb → only before a feminine adjective starting with a consonant / h aspiré.

questions.text: **Pronom 3.**  Ces livres sont ………… pour vous.
solution: *livres* = masculine plural → **tous** pour vous (the final s is pronounced).
questions.idea: Tout: determiner → agrees with the noun · pronoun → agrees with what it stands for · adverb → only before a feminine adjective starting with a consonant / h aspiré.
